description: Stop the cycle of event planner burnout. Learn how to identify the hidden costs of administrative work and use your Mac tools to build a sustainable career.
intro: Event planner burnout is a pervasive crisis driven by the hidden administrative burden of coordinating complex logistics. If you feel physically and mentally exhausted, you are not alone, as up to 88 percent of event professionals report these symptoms.
tldr: Burnout is often caused by the coordination burden of managing third-party vendors rather than the event work itself.
Planners spend 60 to 70 percent of their time on administrative tasks, which is the primary driver of exhaustion.
You can reduce stress by moving to turnkey vendors and automating repetitive data entry tasks.
Lazur helps by acting as a voice-controlled assistant to speed up your daily Mac workflows.

blocks.text: The hidden cost of event planner burnout

The true cost of event planner burnout goes beyond missing sleep. It is a financial and operational drain on your business. You spend 18 hours every week chasing forms, updating spreadsheets, and managing vendor inconsistencies. This is time you cannot bill for. When you are burned out, your decision-making slows down. A single error in a run of show or a miscommunication with a vendor can cost thousands. The emotional toll is just as high. Many planners describe a feeling of constant availability. You never truly switch off because the next email or vendor request is always waiting.

Burnout in this industry is rarely about the event itself. It is about the coordination burden. You are often the middleman for 8 to 15 different vendors per event. Each vendor requires follow-ups, contract reviews, and logistics checks. If one vendor fails to deliver, the entire project timeline shifts. This requires you to pivot constantly. The post-event comedown is another factor. You spend months in a high-stakes, adrenaline-fueled state. When the event ends, your body experiences a sudden crash. This transition is jarring. It disrupts your sleep and recovery cycles.
Practical fixes to reduce your workload

items: Transition to turnkey vendors who handle their own setup and breakdown.
Set strict communication windows like no work emails after 6 PM.
Automate your data entry processes to avoid manual spreadsheet work.
Schedule mandatory recovery days between large events.
Use a centralized hub for all vendor and event data.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you stay focused

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you handle administrative tasks without needing to switch windows or dig through menus. When you are buried in email or project management tools, you can use voice commands to find information. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. Lazur reads the context and answers out loud. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your focus on the task. If you need to find a specific vendor contract, ask Lazur where it is. It will draw a circle around the file, saving you time. For writing, hold fn to dictate clean text directly into your apps. This reduces the time you spend typing repetitive responses to clients.

faq.question: Is event planning really that stressful?
faq.answer: Yes. Research shows that up to 88 percent of event managers experience burnout. The constant coordination of vendors and the high-stakes nature of live events make it one of the most stressful professions.

faq.question: How can I reduce my administrative workload?
faq.answer: Focus on automating data entry and using a centralized project management tool. Moving to turnkey vendors who manage their own logistics also significantly reduces the coordination burden.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with all my Mac apps?
faq.answer: Lazur works on your Mac by seeing your screen and hearing your voice. It does not need specific app integrations. You can use it in any app that runs on macOS.
